title: Foundations of Physical Therapy Evaluation I
description: Psychomotor skills in observation and evaluation of movement.

title: Foundations of Physical Therapy Evaluation II
description: Problem solving and psychomotor skills to perform general physical examination. Concepts, procedures, and techniques required to provide safe and effective patient care.

title: Clinical Anatomy I
description: Applied anatomy of upper and lower extremities of the human body; joint anatomy and mechanics, anatomical structures to produce articular movement to include muscles, arterial, peripheral nervous systems, and articular and extremity movement patterns.

title: Clinical Anatomy II
description: Axial portion of the human body; biomechanics of the spinal column to include head and neck, thorax, related viscera, and abdomino-pelvic region.

title: Professional Skills Development Series I
description: Professional skills development for the novice clinician in physical therapy practice.

title: Professional Skills Development Series II
description: Advanced professional skills development for the novice clinician in physical therapy practice.

title: Professional Skills Development Series III
description: Advanced professional skills development for the intermediate clinician in physical therapy practice.

title: Professional Skills Development IV
description: This is the fourth course in a five-course series that progressively builds upon the clinical skills and mindsets critical for clinical success as autonomous DPT practitioners. This series focuses on: Leadership & Professionalism, Clinical Reasoning, Communication, Teamwork, and Educating Others.

title: Professional Skills Development V
description: This is the fifth course of a five-course series that progressively builds upon the clinical skills and mindsets critical for clinical success as autonomous DPT practitioners. This series focuses on: Leadership & Professionalism, Clinical Reasoning, Communication, Teamwork, and Educating Others.

title: Concepts in Physiology, Pathophysiology, and Pharmacology
description: Normal physiology, diseases, disorders, and injuries. Pathological processes, specific organ system pathology, multisystem pathology, and pharmacological concepts.

title: Neurosciences
description: Anatomy and physiology of central nervous system; substrates and processes of movement.

title: Therapeutic Modalities
description: Anatomy, physiology, pathology, mutability of human biological tissues in the rehabilitation process.

title: Therapeutic Exercise
description: Therapeutic exercise as it applies to clinical practice of physical therapy.

title: Advanced Therapeutic Exercise
description: Advanced principles of therapeutic exercise and its application to physical therapy clinical practice.

title: Initial Clinical Experience
description: Cognitive, psychomotor, and affective skills of physical therapy practice in a clinical setting.

title: Life Cycle I
description: Age-related changes from young adulthood to senescence; analysis of resultant functional limitations.

title: Life Cycle II
description: Normal and delayed maturation processes from conception through adulthood; nervous, cardiovascular, and musculoskeletal systems.

title: Musculoskeletal Therapeutics I
description: Clinical concepts and principles for the diagnosis, examination, and management of musculoskeletal disorders involving the cranio-cervical region, thoracic region, and upper extremities.

title: Musculoskeletal Therapeutics II
description: Clinical principles and concepts for the diagnosis, examination, and management of musculoskeletal disorders involving the lumbosacral region and lower extremities.

title: Interventions in Musculoskeletal Therapeutics
description: Analysis of interventions used to treat clients with dysfunctions of the musculoskeletal system.

title: Cardiopulmonary Therapeutics
description: Electrocardiography, exercise testing, and exercise prescription for patient populations suffering from acute or chronic illness.

title: Neurophysiological Therapeutics I
description: Neurological deficits in adults and children secondary to upper motor-neuron dysfunction.

title: Neurophysiological Therapeutics II
description: Scientific theory pertaining to composite impairments of neurologic patients, with application of motor-control theory to neurorehabilitation.

title: Interventions in Neuromuscular Therapeutics
description: Interventions used to treat clients with dysfunctions of the neuromuscular system.

title: Prosthetics and Orthotics
description: Design, fabrication, and fitting of orthotic and prosthetic devices.

title: Physical Therapy Organization and Administration
description: Designing, equipping, and staffing a physical therapy practice or department. Budget development, cost accounting, supervisory functions, evaluation techniques, and quality assurance. Business strategies and skills for practice setting. Local, national, economic, and political pressures on delivery of physical therapy services.

title: Medical Therapeutics in Physical Therapy Practice
description: Contemporary medical interventions for physical therapy practice.

title: Psychosocial Aspects of Rehabilitation
description: Adjustment to physical disability and terminal illness. Development of communication and ethical decision-making skills.

title: Differential Diagnosis in Physical Therapy
description: Musculoskeletal conditions, medical pathological problems, and/or co-morbidities affecting clinical decision-making.

title: Evidence-Based Practice I: Principles and Clinical Applications
description: Preparation as a consumer of the professional literature in physical therapy.

title: Evidence-Based Practice II: Research Applications
description: Use of evidence in current physical therapy practice.

title: Seminar in Case Presentations
description: Patient case and analysis of evidence from clinical interactions between student and client.

title: Functional Neuro-Biomechanical Relationships
description: Structures of the musculoskeletal system and individual functional regions. Forces sustained in normal and pathological conditions.

title: Preparation for Clinical Education: Concepts and Advocacy
description: Professional physical therapy clinical education and advocacy at individual and societal levels.

title: Evidence-Based Practice IV: Advanced Clinical Reasoning
description: Integrate evidence, patient values, and clinical expertise to critically analyze clinical decision making for complex patient cases across broad range of practice settings.

title: Doctoral Project Part I
description: Requires students to integrate evidence, patient values, and clinical expertise with ICF model of clinical reasoning for actual patient cases. Students will identify and answer focused questions regarding examination, intervention, and prognosis through literature searches and online collegial discussion forums.

title: Doctoral Project Part II
description: Requires students to integrate evidence, patient values, and clinical expertise with the ICF model of clinical reasoning for actual patient case. Students must submit scientific abstract based on clinical case and orally defend their patient case during a poster presentation.

title: Clinical Internship
description: Clinical internship in physical therapy.

title: Terminal Clinical Internship
description: This terminal clinical internship course is designed to synthesize information and skills developed in the final didactic education portion of the curriculum, and incorporate knowledge and clinical skills obtained during the first short term initial clinical experience (DPT 801) and initial long-term clinical internship (DPT 895A).
